_about: Components: the kit a machine's die is made of. Each is exactly one entry on the die (its face: the engine's word for one entry). Nothing generic exists: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. A component a chassis lists under fixed is built in and is never bought or crafted, which is what makes it unique. Every number inside a fight is single digits or low tens since the stock pass's landing (22 October: a blow 1 to 6, big guns to 10; docs/rules.md; the brief retired: git show a550c2e:docs/briefs/stock_pass.md): magnitudes, not steps, any whole number. A rolled entry carries power and power_max and rolls between them; a flat entry is one number and involves no roll. There are no crits. Keywords are a list; authored entries should stay under the validator's cap, upgrades may push past it. passive is null or one object, same shape as a chassis passive. tags are build flavour from the working set (ballistic, missile, beam, plasma, flame, arc, blade, melee), shown in the codex and read only by a module or a passive (and melee by the screen's lunge); the validator holds them to the set, assigned by each piece's fantasy. A face's kind makes it a weapon (attack: spent on a foe, need not deal damage) or equipment (shield, vent: spent on a machine); equipment may carry targets, self_ally (the default), self or ally, and its main icon on the die holds three hexes (the middle its own machine, a filled one a machine it may be spent on); a reach over every foe or every ally is a keyword, every_foe or every_ally. design.stage is draft until Ryan signs the entry off as final; nothing is final yet. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry), flavour (a quote); both still to be written. design is internal and never shown: fantasy, niche, stage, and notes only where the engine still owes something. Numbers are placeholders. A component the engine cannot run yet carries "status": "planned": it is kept, its face is checked for shape, a keyword the vocabulary names but the engine lacks is allowed on it, and the die builds it without that keyword. tier (bible section 10): every component that is not locked carries its tier, 0 to 3. Tier zero is the basics, whose blueprints a run starts with, and the capital's maker makes none; tiers one to three are found, or brought by a bought chassis, and a chassis stocks only components below its own tier (the validator checks both). A component locked on a chassis has none. shape is the silhouette class the model wears when the component is fitted (hardpoints are gun mounts on the model, and a component with a shape takes the next mount in the die's order): barrel, twin_barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, every one points forward) or dish (a projector, for equipment that can look like a gun: shield projectors, a buff coil); none for what is applied to the whole machine and shows nowhere (armour panels, vents). Each class is built by tools/lowforge in every maker's metal (art/models/shapes); the validator holds it to that list.

design.fantasy: Two swings a round if the dice agree. Ghouls in threes.
design.niche: The chase spend against a boss (Ryan, 15 October: "keep it as the chase spend for bosses, tuning as necessary"): two strikes and no area since 31 October, flat 3 a strike, the least that still damages a boss carrying 2; it digs two loads a foe it damages, the most efficient fill and not the most effective weapon.

design.fantasy: As many missiles as it could carry. The box on the Badger's deck.
design.niche: Minerva's indirect fire: the tank that reaches the back rank.

entries.name: Bullion Fragmenter
entries.codex: A sawed-off cannon fed from a crusher hopper.

design.fantasy: One big round. Warm barrel.
design.niche: Fires half the hopper (Ryan, 15 October: "Fragmenter can start by losing 5 stacks, so half of max"): two loads at +2 since 31 October, 8 with both, the plate they stood for spent with them.

entries.name: Slugthrower
entries.codex: Minerva's standard gun. It throws a slug.

design.fantasy: The basic Minervan line weapon: a play on flamethrower under Minerva's trope that things have to physically hit other things.
design.niche: Minerva's rolled line gun, a step above the basics.

design.fantasy: Reliable, unremarkable, always there.
A beam that goes through the wall and the thing hiding behind it.
Small, rude, lands behind the front rank.
Fins. Lots of fins.
design.refit: Retired by the refit pass (landed 10 November): no pure recovery entry stays on the die, cooling is the chassis's. Kept as a draft, undealt; the engine's plain vent until the kinds go.

design.fantasy: The back rank's problem, twice per die.
Lands, then keeps landing.
Whatever it was about to do, it is not doing it now.
Kestrel removed the safety interlock and called it a feature.
design.niche: Ignores armour, a rule written on the piece since Breach was cut on our side (15 November). The one tier-one find that does, so its tier is the component pass's (Ryan: "the player armour piercing pieces should be higher tier, obviously, or gated, I think. Else they become obvious best faces for certain domains"; "Railgun might need to move up a tier regardless just because there won't be room for an even higher damage, even hotter gun").

design.fantasy: For finishing what someone else started.
design.niche: The assassin's finisher: flat, and it grows with the target's missing HP, so the die shows what it will deal to the foe it is held over.

design.fantasy: A pinion is a wing's flight feathers, and a gear: the gun at each wing tip that finishes what the Kite's opening left.
design.niche: The Kite's lock, its finisher (Ryan, 11 November: "maybe it gains it's execution mechanism back so the kite has a finisher to pair with its opener of choice", in a simpler form than the Coriolis Accelerator's slope, which keeps the missing-HP growth in the pool: "two execute pieces can exist"): two shots, one from each wing tip, each doubled against a foe at half its HP or less, read as the die is spent. With the Kite's passive it doubles on the unhurt too, never both at once. Until then its reset gun (21 October).

design.fantasy: Lightning that picks its own second target.
A very expensive bubble.
design.refit: Undealt since the refit pass landed (10 November), until the component pass makes it what the audit says: a Barrier, Rapid, a round's cooldown; the name stands (a deflector turns one blow).

design.fantasy: A shadow falls across the target and it forgets what it was about to do.
design.niche: The ungated Suppress, the Arsenal's at tier three, priced in Volatile in place of heat; no chassis stocks it.

design.fantasy: The left pod on the Baboon's backpack: a loop of borrowed time thrown over an ally, so the harm it took never quite happened and every foe lining it up finds its plan has changed. The name is the session's, his go of 12 November ("Your names are fine").
design.niche: The Baboon's first locked piece (Ryan, 11 November: "Cleanse an ally. Disrupt all enemies targeting it. -> upgrades buff the ally or improve the debuff"; "Disrupt: yes that was the point. It applies Disrupt the effect. Targeting all means targeting the ally. Cleanse can be self, sure, unless it needs a nerf"): on itself or an ally, a Cleanse, and every foe showing intent on it, a blow at every machine included, takes Disrupt, its next move in its list, aimed where it was.

design.fantasy: The right pod on the Baboon's backpack: light stretched long until there is nothing left in it, so whatever it touches is worth less, its buffs and its blows alike. The name is the session's, his go of 12 November ("Your names are fine").
design.niche: The Baboon's second locked piece (Ryan, 11 November: "Purge 1 and Weaken 1. -> upgrades buff a weak ally, or improve the purge and weaken"; "Indirect for the second piece"): equipment on any foe, a buff stripped and a Sapped laid, the one stack of the Baboon's own that feeds its Paradox.

design.fantasy: Lobbed light. It lands at the same brightness every time and keeps burning.
design.niche: Indirect burn at a flat number: predictable stacks for the passive to read.
design.parked: Off the Baboon on 11 November with its rework and parked, undealt (Ryan: "Solar flare array can get parked, probably better as a tier 2 or something based on the name alone"); its near twin in the pool, the Incendiary Shells, is why it is no ordinary tier-one piece.

design.fantasy: A ring of light that scours whatever the rift left on the metal.
design.niche: The cleanse carrier: shield an ally and clear its statuses. A find, not Aphelion stock.
design.refit: Undealt since the refit pass landed (10 November), until the component pass makes it what the audit says: a Ward and a Cleanse on a machine, renamed the Corona Veil (the engine's Cleanse rides only a shield or a vent today).

design.fantasy: A small fast gun that gives the machine its turn back.
design.niche: The tempo tool: a rapid entry so a control frame gets another look at its die.

design.fantasy: A siren and a strobe on a plate of armour. Everything in earshot comes for it.
design.niche: The accessible lure (damage redirection is common, never a tank's lock): an Indirect debuff with Spread, so a rank turns on its machine for the round.

design.fantasy: It launches a sticky cryo canister with a really annoying beep or something, for the lore reason (Ryan, 18 October). Whatever it sticks to comes for the Polar Bear, and whoever hits the canister gets the cold out of it.
design.niche: The Polar Bear's locked lure, one on its die (Ryan, 9 November: one Flinger and no Rapid, so the lure costs its action): an Indirect debuff with Lure and Cryo, gaining Spread while its machine is sealed (Lockdown's grant), so it turns one foe open and a rank's three sealed. The foe it lures carries Cryo; any machine's hit with a weapon spends every stack and cools the hitter, and the Polar Bear's own weapons hit a foe carrying Cryo 1 harder, so who cashes it is the round's call.

design.fantasy: The Wild Boar's front end: a ram and a plow blade that go through a wall or a rank of fodder at the same speed.
design.niche: The Boar's locked self-defence since 11 November (Ryan: "Breaching plow could easily earn its place by simply being a self-defense that does something else"; "Cleanse self and gain Barrier, cooldown 1"): it clears the Boar's debuffs and puts a Barrier up, and the passive turns that Barrier into Breach on the next gun it fires. Until then a Direct 4 Spread 2 cleave that braced 2. Since 15 November that gun ignores armour, a written rule where Breach stood.

design.fantasy: A drum-fed scattergun on a pintle, its shells bursting into a rank of foes. Fire, and the car is already moving. Ryan, 19 October: "a low damage, spread, maybe rapid, weapon with a new debuff: flak".
design.niche: The Prairie Dog's locked gun and the maker's first Brittle piece: a flat low blow that sprays the target's rank and lays Brittle on each foe hit, so the team's many small blows land harder and the car takes less from the foes that carry it (its passive). The softener's round: spray, then the four cash. Ryan, 11 November: "turn the Flak repeater into a Flak weapon and not a bad spread weapon"; "1 damage, Flak 2, cooldown 1. Heat not sure. But that prevents it from being the chase every round and stacking on itself." Its Spread kept as it stood, his to cut.

design.fantasy: A barbed dart on a cable that opens inside whatever it pins and keeps the wound open. Ryan, 11 November: kept "since it's such a stupid and neat silhouette", and named by him (the Megataser Harpoon until then, its Shock gone to the Translocator).
design.niche: The Dingo's Brittle piece (Ryan, 11 November: "the obvious hole I see in the W&S lineup ... is another Flak orbit. The harpoon could be that synergy"; "Applies 1 flak and the target's flak does not decay this round", the pin "the better shape"): it lays Brittle 1 and holds every stack on its target through the round's end, so the team's Brittle builds on one foe, a boss most of all. Reading Brittle twice is "a better upgrade for something".

design.fantasy: Not a winch (Ryan, 19 October: a cable cannot swap two things, and the maker cannot go that low-tech) but a teleporter in the maker's register, "guys this totally isn't just a teleporter". The name is his working one.
design.niche: The Dingo's second locked piece (Ryan's go, 19 October; the bible's Dingo row): pick two foes, or a foe and an empty slot, and they trade places; no damage. It exposes a caster to Direct fire, sets the acting order and bunches foes for every area piece, a cross-maker combo in one locked piece; a massive foe fills its column and stays, so bosses are out by rule; a swap with an empty front slot is a pull. Shock since 11 November (Ryan: "I like putting Shock on the translocator since that makes it not dead versus only frontliners and versus massives and bosses that can't be swapped"): it takes two targets always, both come out Shocked, and a massive foe named stays where it stands ("Translocator should still target two, always. Confusing UX otherwise").

design.fantasy: The Buzzard's engines fire forward for one shot. The hotter the airframe, the bigger the shot, and the airframe is cold afterwards.
design.niche: The Buzzard's burst: spend the heat the passive was living on.

design.fantasy: Fists, and a temper: every hit the Nemesis takes, its own included, is another swing it gets to throw.
design.niche: The Nemesis's locked melee and its rage's outlet: with five rage banked it goes out charged, unasked, spends them and is Instant, its die rolling again, itself included, so a fist may show again (Ryan, 12 November: "backtrack on the Nemesis and give the fists Instant again, reserving the Breach for an upgrade"; "Each reroll costs 5 rage. Just swapping the Breach for Instant, everything else stays the same"). The roll again was its signature from 12 October to 11 November, a rage a roll; the Breach on five rage, the tank buster's punch of 11 November, is one direction of its upgrades.

design.fantasy: Fists that weigh what the Arsenal says they weigh. Each blow burns, and each blow costs the machine a little of itself.
design.niche: Shelved: a tier-three blueprint kept unstocked until the gravity piece returns (the bible's Nemesis fists row).
design.parked: Back in design since 15 November, undealt, as the blade class retired: a gauntlet on a machine with no hands was the headache (Ryan, 14 November: "we didn't want to deal with the headache of how something with no hands wields a gauntlet"), so it returns renamed as a short-range gun, melee in the tag's sense, or stays here (Ryan, 15 November: "renamed into short range (i.e 'melee' as per our definition) guns, or just sent back to design"). Its class a barrel meanwhile, a gun's.

design.fantasy: Four blades on four arms, cutting as one. What they cut loose from the fallen the machine takes in; the Arsenal's manual calls it attunement.
design.niche: The Ammit's locked melee, one entry since its rework (Ryan, 12 November: "The 4 claws are combined into one weapon that deals 1x4 instead, with Breach. They no longer gain Empowered on kill"): four strikes of 1 at one foe, past its armour, so every stack of Empowered counts four times on it. Four copies of a flat 3 that Empowered a kill until then. Its Breach is the written rule, ignores armour, since the keyword was cut on our side (15 November).

design.fantasy: The reactor's tap opened the other way: what the Ammit has taken in, burned for a round. Ryan's piece, 12 November, and his name for it of 15 November (the Soul Siphon until then).
design.niche: The Ammit's second lock, equipment spent on itself (Ryan, 12 November: "Consume up to 5 souls, granting 1 Empowered per soul. Cooldown 3"; "No Empowered decays this round. And I mean none, not ally or enemy"): the round it is spent the Ammit does nothing else, and the next it swings at everything it held and what it consumed, whole. Unplayable with no Essence. Its cooldown keeps the hold from chaining. The foes' Empowered is held too, its price against a rally. Its hold is a buff on the Ammit since 15 November, Essence Flare (Ryan: "an Ammit specific buff. I would give it to the Ammit only, even though it affects the whole battlefield"), so a Purge that takes the buff ends the hold.

design.fantasy: Mining kit with the safety plate off. It puts a rivet through anything.
design.niche: Minerva's starter gun.

design.fantasy: The gun every Kestrel airframe leaves the factory with. Light, flat, warm.
design.niche: Kestrel's starter gun.

design.fantasy: A jet's bleed-air valve thrown wide open: the engine dumps its own heat overboard. The jet's brake.
design.niche: Kestrel's basic self vent, the bigger number of the two basic vents, self only.
design.refit: Retired by the refit pass (landed 10 November): no pure recovery entry stays on the die. Kept as a draft, undealt.

design.fantasy: A ring of hard light thrown round a machine for the one blow that matters. Nothing clever about it, which Aphelion resents.
design.niche: The Barrier basic, Aphelion's one basic: the next blow a foe lands on the machine deals no damage, until the round's end; on itself or an ally. It was the Halo Shield, a shield of 6, until shields left the die (the refit pass, landed 10 November).

design.fantasy: Kestrel's answer to a regulator: a coil that pushes an ally's guns past the line for one round.
design.niche: The first buff component: two stacks of Empowered on a machine for the round.

design.fantasy: A deep-space radiator, unfolded. Heat goes where it always went: out.
design.niche: Aphelion's ally vent at tier one.
design.refit: Retired by the refit pass (landed 10 November): cooling an ally is the Puffin's by Ryan's direction. Kept as a draft, undealt.

design.fantasy: The Arsenal's issue weapon, older than it looks: plasma loaded like powder, and no two shots alike.
design.niche: The Arsenal's starter gun.

design.fantasy: A stream of plasma that sticks. Purification, the manual says.
design.niche: The Arsenal's starter burn.

design.fantasy: Plasma lobbed high and falling burning.
design.niche: The Arsenal's hot Indirect burn.

design.fantasy: Heat condensed and thrown away. Nobody outside the Arsenal knows where.
design.niche: The Arsenal's vent: the biggest number, paid in hull, so on the Nemesis every spend banks a rage.
design.refit: Back in design with the Arsenal's sessions since the refit pass landed (10 November), undealt (Claude's lean: its heat thrown at a foe as a blow, paid in hull: a weapon).

design.fantasy: A beam drawn off the reactor's own surface. It burns what it touches and the machine with it.
design.niche: The Stingray's locked piece since 11 November (Ryan: "target ally or self. The enemy directly in front of them gets the debuff, or if none in either rank in front, the closest column that does, searching left -right-left-right"; "I don't think it should deal damage"; "The stingray wasn't intended as an offensive only unit. The interesting take here is a defensive debuff plus an offensive buff. Normally the opposite are paired together, a defend buff with a status that damages while you're defended. Flipping the script is neat. Upgrades can redirect it to the primed+burn abuse as one of the branches"): spent on itself or an ally, Empowered there and Sapped on the foe in front of it (his name for the status, "Let's use Sapped"), both deepened by the Suite. Still hot, so the Suite has heat to read. Until then a Direct 4 Burn 2 gun, the Blazethrower's twin.

design.fantasy: A lattice of light laid over a machine's weapons. Everything it hits afterwards keeps burning.
design.niche: Aphelion's buff: a stack of Primed, on itself or an ally, so the next weapon that machine fires carries Ablate 1 (one more a strike on an Ablate gun) and the Stingray's suite has a buff to deepen as well as its burns. A primer since 15 November, a stack a weapon fired; for the round, on every blow, until then. Its one stack is a placeholder.

entries.name: Backwash Ionizer
entries.codex: Ionizes the target's backwash, temporarily increasing the target's shield capacity until round end.

design.fantasy: The whole front of the Puffin is one shield projector, and it only points outward.
design.niche: The Puffin's locked shield: a big bubble it can only raise on an ally, and the game's first Overshield, so it may lift the ally past its maximum for the round (Ryan, 2 October: a shield specialist, not a shield-bot; 5 October: overshield a rare keyword, the projector first). Overshield was cut as a keyword on 15 November (Ryan's mark), so it raises no shield past the maximum: its session finds it another rule.

design.fantasy: A probe lobbed into the formation. Whatever the thing it lands beside was about to do, it now differentiates.
design.niche: The first Disrupt in the pool: an indirect debuff that turns a foe onto its other move. It deals nothing, so it counts for Aphelion's Sponsorship.

design.fantasy: Whatever the rift left on the metal goes straight from solid to gone, with the heat.
design.niche: Aphelion's cleanse vent at tier one, where the Corona Shield is the tier-two cleanse shield.
design.refit: Undealt since the refit pass landed (10 November), until the component pass makes it what the audit says: a Cleanse on itself or an ally, equipment (the engine's Cleanse rides only a shield or a vent today).

design.fantasy: It projects polarity. Nobody at Aphelion will say what that means, and the next thing to hit the target hits twice as hard.
design.niche: The first Shock: a line debuff that sets up a doubled blow for the team; Shocked is a status, so it feeds the Baboon's Pocket Paradox.

design.fantasy: A hydraulic pit prop jammed under a machine's plating. It holds the roof up in the mine; it holds the armour on out here.
design.niche: Armoured for the round on itself or an ally: the answer to volume (swarms, multi-strikes, a storm of small blows), nothing against a breach. The Armoured basic at tier zero since the refit pass landed (10 November), in the Canopy's place.

design.fantasy: The falling-object guard over a mining machine's cab, swung down to cover the frame: what keeps a cave-in off the pilot keeps a blow off the hull.
design.niche: Minerva's basic self shield, the bigger number of the two basic shields, self only.
design.refit: Retired by the refit pass (landed 10 November): shields left the die and the Shoring Jack took its place among the basics. Kept as a draft, undealt, until the component pass removes it (Ryan: 'Canopy was always a little lame').

design.fantasy: Mining gauntlets with the arc welder left switched on. What they punch stays live.
design.niche: Melee that Shocks what it hits and leaves standing, so the next blow on it lands double.
design.parked: Back in design since 15 November, undealt, as the blade class retired: a gauntlet on a machine with no hands was the headache (Ryan, 14 November: "we didn't want to deal with the headache of how something with no hands wields a gauntlet"), so it returns renamed as a short-range gun, melee in the tag's sense, or stays here (Ryan, 15 November: "renamed into short range (i.e 'melee' as per our definition) guns, or just sent back to design"). Its class a barrel meanwhile, a gun's.

design.fantasy: A ward projected from the machine's own reactor, paid for out of its frame. The manual calls it devotion.
design.niche: The biggest shield in the pool, paid in the spender's hull: raised on an ally, the Arsenal machine bleeds to cover a friend.
design.refit: Back in design with the Arsenal's sessions since the refit pass landed (10 November), undealt: what its hull buys when it is no shield (Claude's lean: a Barrier on an ally that holds until it is struck).

design.fantasy: A censer swung over the hull. Whatever strikes the consecrated metal is marked for what comes next.
design.niche: Back in design (Ryan, 15 November: "Send the retribution thurible back to design. It can have unique text but not until we sort out our fundamentals"), a planned draft nothing deals. It was the Retaliate carrier: for two rounds, a foe that strikes the machine's bare hull is Shocked; on the Nemesis its own punches spent the shocks. Retaliate was cut as a buff word the same day, so its rule will be the piece's own text.

design.fantasy: A minigun, but more. Three bursts a pull, each rolled on its own.
design.niche: The multi-strike horde gun: three small blows that each roll and proc on their own, strong into bare foes and with Primed, poor into armour.

design.fantasy: A diffuser on the exhaust that spreads the wake thin. It runs cooler, and somehow faster.
design.niche: A combined entry: a vent that also shields, so a support entry is never a dead roll and costs its turn like any other.
design.refit: Back in design since the refit pass landed (10 November), undealt: two recoveries on one piece; its own line points at heat turned into tempo, a payoff vent as equipment.

design.fantasy: A canister of wire and resin lobbed at a foe's feet (Ryan's working name). It bursts as the round ends, and the foe beside it is caught in the same net.
design.niche: The funnel-web's locked control, kept as hard control under the stun row (Ryan, 17 October: it fits the kit): a double Suppress on a delay, the webbed foe and the foe beside it each losing its next turn as the round ends, no damage, no cooldown (Ryan, 16 November: "moved to End of Round and be repositioned as a double suppress on a delay, not suppress one this turn and one the next"; "The spider is a planner, so removing the reactive tool and rewarding it for thinking ahead is good"). It stops nothing already announced: it buys two silent foes for the next round, which the ambush bites. Until then it burst at the end of the webbed foe's own action, the foe beside it losing that round's action: "almost-not-quite an unconditional suppress on one foe", his.

design.fantasy: The cylinder's motor. Ryan, 18 October: "spin the barrel, rapid, no cooldown, next component gets +5 damage or something"; the drum spins up and the next shot leaves hotter, a minigun's spin-up inside a revolver's cylinder.
design.niche: The Cassowary's locked combo piece: no damage, Instant with no cooldown, no heat and no Volatile (Rapid with a spin of its own until 12 November, when Ryan made the roll that may land on itself a keyword: "the rapid no cooldown pieces change to a new keyword: Instant (reroll after use, can land on itself)"), its roll a true spin of the cylinder over every chamber, itself included; each spin grants a stack of Spun Up for the next weapon spend, carried between turns. Its limiter is the cylinder and its odds: its spin lands on itself one time in six, to be spent again (Ryan, 19 October: "I think we can allow the high-roll for the revolver spin, landing on itself, as an exception to the global rule"), a fifth of a spin more a spend on average, each a stack of Spun Up; every other way back to it in a round runs through the other chambers' switch-offs or the team's rerolls. The chase: spin into a Rapid piece into the Spin-Up into the big gun.

design.fantasy: The Clydesdale's battery lever. Ryan, 11 November: "Each die has the same locked component on it, that flips its die to the other on Rapid, cooldown 1, so it can only flip once a turn": four of its hardpoints stand on the deck and four ride below, and the lever swaps them, the four up pivoting upright and sinking as the four below rise.
design.niche: The Clydesdale's locked piece: no damage, Rapid. Spent on itself it turns the die to its other battery, which stays up from fight to fight, and Rapid's free roll lands on the battery it raised. One entry live on both batteries, so one switch-off and once a round (his "the same piece with one cooldown"): Rapid's own since 12 November, the entry dark for the rest of the round, where it printed a cooldown of 1 under the old count.

design.fantasy: The signal mirror on its mast, turned on one foe with the whole boiler behind it. Ryan, 11 November: the locked piece "takes the buzzards old form. Cools completely, damage per heat spent. Low base damage"; "The heliograph term can go on the new locked piece" (his name of 20 October: "Keep heliographic cause its dumber"). The name is a session's draft he kept (11 November: "Heliographic death ray is a great name. Kept"), and its gun his the same day: "an actual gun. Pipes connecting it to the boiler, steampunk style. Mirror or mirrors as part of it because weird future nonsense tech. Like a steam powered mirrored laser railgun."
design.niche: The Whip Scorpion's answer to one big foe: it fires every point of heat the machine holds as one blow and leaves it cold, a low base and a point for every 2 heat. The same gauge feeds its passive's release, which lands on every foe as it reboots, 1 for every 2 heat (Ryan, 11 November, of the release as a Sweep: "I'd keep the sweep the more attractive option in terms of raw power"; a blow on every foe since the 12th, on the reboot's vent since the 17th), so its heat is the ray on one foe now, its shield kept, or the valves on the whole pack for its turn and a round bare. The Buzzard's Afterburner Cannon held this form until its rework of 11 November.

design.fantasy: Every foe on the field turns to face it, and it braces. The Whip Scorpion's Heliographic Siphon of 20 October with its heat left behind. A session's name, kept on his word of 12 November ("The working names are fine").
design.niche: Ryan, 11 November: "Lure every foe, gain armour is a massive premium component for Minerva chassis. If that's allowed to exist as a component, it needs to be tier 3 Minerva, not random W&S. And the name needs to change if it's no longer gaining heat on the component." Dealt on his word of 12 November: "The Minervan lure all can exist in tier 3, sure."

design.fantasy: A heat ray in the old sense, the one that walks across a field on three legs (Ryan, 20 October: "Thermal Ray gives me war-of-the-worlds vibes"). The hottest shot a spend can make, and the pressure it leaves is the point.
design.niche: The Whip Scorpion's stock gun and fuel: Direct, flat and hot, so one shot banks the heat its reboot's vent fires. A hot slot-in for any machine that runs hot on purpose.

design.fantasy: The hangar deck's mooring field thrown over the squad; charged, the shutters close and the squad is gone from the fight for a round.
design.niche: The Swallowtail's dock, locked: a shield to every ally (the team shield, the first in the game, honest by its number); spending a muster instead Phases every ally that has not acted this round, no cooldown.
design.notes: 15 November: Phased is granted as the round ends and stands through the next (Ryan's mark; the bible's Phased row), so the charged form queues it and the allies keep their dice. Every granter of ours is to be gated ("it should be earned"): this piece's gate and its reach are its machine's session's.

design.fantasy: The observer's flare over the target: every gun on the field finds it. Charged, it bursts in the foe's face.
design.niche: The Swallowtail's spotter, locked: the foe it lights is Exposed (the Kestrel session's debuff: in every machine's Direct reach and its armour counting for nothing, through the next round), no damage; spending a muster Suppresses it too, a stun gated by the price and clocked by Numbed.

design.fantasy: A crane, a hose and a crate of plate lowered onto an ally in the middle of the fight. Charged, the whole tender comes down.
design.niche: The Swallowtail's resupply, locked: a shield and some cooling on an ally; spending a muster instead fills its shield to the maximum, cools it to zero and cleanses it.

design.fantasy: The bugle that wakes the camp. Charged, it gets a machine back on its feet and firing.
design.niche: The Swallowtail's rally, locked: the team gains a reroll this round; spending a muster instead lets an ally act again (its die rolled again and spent again, the gun platform's engine).

design.fantasy: A cluster howitzer whose shells burst over a rank, and whose spent casings the forge pulls back as ammo. Ryan, 21 October: "a cluster cannon that does low damage, spreads Flak 1 to all targets hit, and returns 1 ammo for each target hit". The name is Claude's, Ryan's pick: shrapnel is the old-world cluster round, and a recuperator is the real artillery part that returns the barrel after recoil, here returning the shells.
design.niche: The Musk Ox's status and ammo piece: a low number on up to four foes (Spread 1 and Penetrate 1, Splash until the word was cut on 15 November), Brittle 1 on each for the team's blows that turn, and 1 ammo back for every foe it hits, so a crowd fills the magazine and a lone boss is a wash.

design.fantasy: The rocket racks emptied at once, every tube, at nothing in particular. Ryan, 21 October: random targeting and Spread and Penetrate on every strike, "the area-suppressing-fire-artillery fantasy of obliterating all the trash via repeated AOE damage"; "The artillery piece isn't a precision weapon". The name is the order to spend everything, in the maker's dry voice (Ryan's pick of Claude's: abstract and military, nothing to do with the hardware).
design.niche: The Musk Ox's salvo. A stand-in since Sweep went (12 November; Ryan: "gating the Scorp and Musk Ox to needing 8 heat/ammo to fire their specials, and making them a 'target all'"; "Ox will be tackled in a seperate session"): it needs 8 ammo, empties the magazine and lands its number on every foe. Its numbers, and whether it scales with the magazine, are that session's.

design.fantasy: A crash reload: the forge run hot to cast a few shells at once, the heat dumped into the hull. Ryan, 21 October: "something that reloads but actually gives the machine a good chunk of heat".
design.niche: The Musk Ox's tempo piece, in for testing: Rapid, 2 ammo, and heat its low maximum feels, so with the foes' Scorched it threatens an overheat.

design.fantasy: Length contraction shrinks the space between, so every Mine on the field ends on one foe (Ryan, 21 October, on the pull's name: "something about warping or teleporting"; he picked this one that day).
design.niche: The Lammergeier's gather (Ryan, 9 November: "moves all mines to a single target, and Exposes that target. The Expose rider will effectively create an AoE expose mine, which we can try and see if it's dangerous."): a debuff that Exposes its target and, in the rider phase, moves every Mine the field's other foes carry onto it, so the team's Direct guns can finish the foe that holds them all and its blast Exposes its neighbours. Never Rapid and no damage of its own, a tool and not a gun. Retired: the pull of 17 October onto a slot, with the slot mines.

design.fantasy: A syrinx is a bird's voice box, where a mimic copies any sound (Ryan named it 21 October): the drone sings the note the Reverberant Payload holds, and the Mine answers it.
design.niche: The Lammergeier's detonator (Ryan, 9 November: "Deals a small amount of damage and detonates a foe's combined mine immediately (or mine stacks, whichever shape we end up with). The small chip damage makes it add a stack first. Try without a cooldown first."): a weapon of chip damage whose spend adds its own Mine first, then blows the target's Mine on it and every foe round it. Alone it is a small Splash gun; on a gathered Mine it is the cash-out. Its chip spends a Shock on the target, so a Shock doubles the chip, never the Mine. Retired: the mark of 21 October (the next weapon to kill the foe left its shot in the empty slot), with the slot mines.

design.fantasy: Named by Ryan, 11 November. The seabird's dive: the strafer comes round again faster than its own shots.
design.niche: The Skua's lock (Ryan, 11 November: "Gain a stack of Ricochet, Rapid"; "Rapid, cooldown 1, the only way to get more than one ricochet a round"): spent on itself it gains a stack of Ricochet and its die rolls again, the Swoop dark for the rest of its round. One entry in four, so it is what makes the ramp felt in a short fight.

design.fantasy: A pod of darts (Ryan named it 21 October; 12 November: "Flechette to me sounds like something that hits a bunch of times, like a machine gun").
design.niche: Reworked 12 November with Sweep's removal (Ryan: "the flechette pod just needs a rework. Doesn't have to be tied to the skua ... It could be the simple tier 1 multi-hit, maybe 1x3?"; then, the Maxigun being 2 by 3 at tier one already, "Flechette could be 1x4"): four strikes of 1 at one foe. It carries riders and flat buffs four times and a point of armour stops it whole. Its heat is the heat pass's ("Not worried about heat till the heat pass"), left at the 1 it had. Still in the Skua's stock.

design.fantasy: St. Elmo's fire on the mast (Ryan named it 21 October): a beacon that draws the foe's eye, its glow the heat that mends the shield.
design.niche: The Storm Petrel's lock since its rework of 17 November: a debuff, Indirect, heat 3; the foe it is spent on is Lured for the round, and its heat stands up shield through the Riot Field Generator, so the taunt is its own mending. Its branches tweak it (the chassis's branches): the Defence direction's Hardened and then Spread with a stack for each foe lured, the Striker's Charged and then Chain 3.
design.notes: Built 30 October as a lure of no heat laying Regenerating 3 on its own machine (regenerates), the rider that left the engine with it on 17 November; a lure that runs hot in its place, his "Your verdict leans are solid" to the lean of the same day.

design.fantasy: A falcon's eye has two foveae, the deep one for distance (Ryan named it 21 October): the spotter's sensor ball, lit as it paints.
design.niche: The Needletail's lock: a debuff, Indirect, that Exposes the foe it reaches through the next round (in every machine's Direct reach, its armour counting for nothing; refreshed, never added). A setup, so Rapid on its machine once a round, and the paint the team's Direct guns cash.

design.fantasy: The Immelmann turn reverses a fighter's course and climbs (Ryan named it 21 October), as a spent ally comes round to act again: the flagship's eight boosters, lit.
design.niche: The Giant Petrel's first lock, Rapid (Ryan, 21 October): spent on itself the team gains a reroll; spent on an ally whose die is spent, three of the team's rerolls are paid, banked or fresh, and the ally's die rolls again, never onto the entry it showed, and it acts again. The order is the play: spend the ally first.
design.notes: Built 30 October: the self use is the Reveille Horn's reroll for the team (a rule of its own since 15 November, the Rallied buff cut); the ally use (ally_action, the Horn's charged act-again priced in rerolls) takes an ally whose die is spent while the team holds the price, and its Rapid gives the Petrel its turn back.

design.fantasy: Spray blown off the wave crests its missiles skim (Ryan named it 21 October): the ekranoplan's launch tubes on its back.
design.niche: The Giant Petrel's second lock, the battery (Ryan, 21 October: "your battery shape, works well"): a rolled Indirect gun; if its shot kills, the team gains two rerolls this round, banked if unspent. The gamble is Kestrel's: the range against the foe's hull is on the die, and a kill brews most of the Booster's price.
design.notes: Built 30 October: the kill rider (kill_rerolls) adds to the round's rerolls once a spend that kills, and the bank keeps what goes unspent.

design.fantasy: Reheat is the afterburner (Ryan named it 21 October), sent to an ally over the flagship's uplink.
design.niche: The Giant Petrel's third lock, a buff (Ryan, 21 October): an ally gains Empowered 2 and its die rolls again, never onto the entry showing; on an ally whose die is spent the roll gives nothing and the Empowered halves to one for next round. A locked piece on a tier three, so it may outdo the Overcharge Coil (Ryan: components grow in power as tiers go up).
design.notes: Built 30 October: the roll on its target (rolls_target), a reroll of that die never onto the entry showing; a spent die rolls nothing.

design.fantasy: A long rifle whose rounds leave the barrel just past the speed of sound.
design.niche: The step between the Laser Carbine and the Overclocked Railgun, Kestrel's 3, 5 and 10: flat, warm and plain.

design.fantasy: A shell fused to burst over a rank, peppering every foe under it with fragments that leave each one easier to hit.
design.niche: The Brittle family's slot-in above the basics: a rolled Indirect spray laying Brittle 1 on a foe and its neighbours, for the team's many small blows to cash.

design.fantasy: A rotary cannon run at its full cyclic rate: four rounds where a rifle fires one.
design.niche: The multi-strike gun (Ryan, 14 October: badly needed), Brittle's partner and the strafer's eight: every strike carries the foe's Brittle and loses its armour.

design.fantasy: An anti-aircraft gun levelled at the ground: one heavy burst that leaves its target ringing for everything after it.
design.niche: The Brittle family's single-target layer: Brittle 2 on one foe for the Maxigun to chew.

design.fantasy: A firebox gun that throws its own coals: the target catches, and so does the machine that fed it.
design.niche: Ablate on the foe and Ablating on its own firer. It was slow fuel by decision while a machine's Burning was heat (22 October); since Ablate (15 November) the price is a point of its own shield a stack and it fuels nothing, the component pass's to read again.

design.fantasy: A charge that pulls the fire out of whatever it strikes and turns it inward: the flames go out, and the foe goes down with them.
design.niche: The fire-synergy stun: it consumes every stack of Ablating on its target for a point a stack, and Suppresses it if it consumed two or more, so one Ablate 2 piece opens it and no all-in ablate team is needed.

design.fantasy: A slab of mine-shaft door on a hydraulic arm, swung across in front of whoever needs it for the one blow that matters.
design.niche: The Barrier carrier: the next blow a foe lands on the machine deals no damage, until the round's end; self or ally, never a team buff (the Barrier row).

design.fantasy: A field that smears a machine's state across the round: whatever strikes it lands, but nothing it carries finds a hold.
design.niche: The Ward carrier: every blow a foe lands on the machine this round leaves no rider, and no silence or purge touches it; self or ally, never a team buff.

entries.name: Null Field Emitter
entries.codex: A debuff. Every buff the foe carries loses two stacks: a brace, a rally's Empowered, a readied return, a primed claw, a barrier, a regrowth, a stun's Numbed. Its abilities stay, a core's guard and a golden rage among them, and a Ward turns it away.
entries.flavour: Decoherence is not destruction. The field simply declines to remember what the subject was doing.

design.fantasy: The Science Vessel's EMP, slottable: Aphelion's physics nonsense unwriting the enemy's state. The jellyfish's EMP, when it lands, carries the same keyword on a blow with Disrupt (the bible's Aphelion row).
design.niche: The strip-it-or-shoot decision at tier two, Indirect so it reaches the commander in the back; stocked by nobody, a blueprint found.
